key_insight: Instead of performing all reasoning up front, "Think Anywhere" interleaves reasoning and code generation so the model can invoke targeted, deeper thinking at the exact points where implementation reveals new complexity. This adaptive, stepwise reasoning leads to more robust and efficient code synthesis.
problem_solved: Upfront-only reasoning is brittle for code generation because many problems only reveal their true difficulty during implementation; the paper addresses the need to allocate reasoning effort adaptively across the generation process.
method: Interleave reasoning and generation: enable the model to trigger localized chain-of-thought whenever the current implementation step is uncertain or fails checks.
Checkpoint-based local planning and verification: use intermediate checkpoints (e.g., tests, compilation feedback, or heuristics) to decide when to pause and reason deeper.
Cost-aware allocation: prioritize reasoning budget to high-uncertainty segments so effort is concentrated where it most improves correctness and efficiency.
impact: Makes LLM-driven code generation more reliable and efficient by focusing reasoning where it matters during implementation, reducing needless computation and lowering bug rates. Practitioners get better trade-offs between latency, cost, and correctness when deploying code-writing models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: generate → detect uncertainty/checkpoint → invoke local reasoning → continue generation
Timeline visualization: code generation steps with variable-height "thinking" bars showing adaptive reasoning intensity
Code editor mockup: code snippets with inline thought-bubbles and verification badges (pass/fail)
Comparison chart: error rate and latency for Upfront Thinking vs Think Anywhere vs No Reasoning
paper_authors: Xue Jiang, Tianyu Zhang, Ge Li, Mengyang Liu, Taozhi Chen
